timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: We run Azure, AWS, and GCP. That's three logins per person?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Only if you're doing identity wrong. One identity provider should rule them all.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Microsoft Entra ID. AWS and GCP become service providers that trust it.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: AWS IAM Identity Center. Entra signs users in, SCIM provisions groups, and group membership maps to IAM roles.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Conditional Access still applies on AWS?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Yes. Every AWS sign-in gets MFA, device checks, and risk evaluation from Entra.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Workforce identity federation. Google trusts Entra, so users bring their existing credentials. No duplicate accounts.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: And machines running on AWS that need Azure resources?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Workload identity federation. They swap their native token for an Azure token. No stored secrets to leak.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So nobody gets orphaned cloud accounts?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. Fire the user in Entra and every cloud loses access instantly.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do we spot over-permissioned cloud roles?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Defender for Cloud. It monitors cross-cloud permissions and flags identities that can do too much.
